definitions.explanation: A friend from the distant past, someone one has known for a long time. Carries a literary, somewhat nostalgic tone and implies a deep, lasting bond.

examples.japanese: {旧友|きゅうゆう}と{再会|さいかい}した。
examples.english: I reunited with an old friend.

examples.japanese: {大学時代|だいがくじだい}の{旧友|きゅうゆう}から{突然|とつぜん}{連絡|れんらく}が{来|き}た。
examples.english: I suddenly got a message from an old college friend.

examples.japanese: {十年|じゅうねん}ぶりに{旧友|きゅうゆう}と{酒|さけ}を{酌|く}み{交|か}わし、{昔話|むかしばなし}に{花|はな}が{咲|さ}いた。
examples.english: I shared drinks with an old friend for the first time in ten years, and we had a wonderful time reminiscing.

notes:
USAGE:
More literary and refined than {古|ふる}い{友達|ともだち} (old friend). Often used in written contexts or when speaking with some formality. Implies a friendship that has endured over many years.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旧友|きゅうゆう}と{再会|さいかい}する (to reunite with an old friend)
- {旧友|きゅうゆう}を{訪|たず}ねる (to visit an old friend)
- {旧友|きゅうゆう}との{絆|きずな} (bond with an old friend)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {幼|おさな}なじみ: childhood friend — specifically someone known since childhood
- {古|ふる}い{友達|ともだち}: old friend — casual, everyday expression
- {親友|しんゆう}: best friend — emphasizes closeness, not duration
